# PGP transfer encoding has signature and backend-specific exceptions

The cleanup regression restored transfer encoding for signed-only PGP/MIME so message transport rewrites cannot invalidate a detached signature. Current code also forces encoding when GPGME signs, including encrypted mail, because that backend can transform UTF-8 bytes. Inline signing remains separate. Newer MimeMessage permits a clean body to remain 7bit for the unobtrusive signature format even when forceMsgEncoding is set; classic multipart signatures retain base64 in the focused test, while non-ASCII, controls and long lines remain encoded. Do not teach a blanket always-base64 rule or infer that a comment about wrapping replaces the current condition. No send transition or cryptographic validation was run.

Scope: openpgp.
